Independent uniform W,U give the stated study with X=1{U<=9/10}, Y0=0, Y1=1{W>=1/2}, and delta=1/20. All ValidStudy conditions hold. The sample event E has probability 2^-100>0. Thus the conditional indicator expectation is one on a genuinely positive covariate event. This witnesses failure of the conditional proof step, not unconditional coverage for constant propensity.

Take W uniform on [0,1], X and Y1 independent Bernoulli(1/2) variables independent of W, Y0=0, pi=m=1/2 and delta=1/4. This satisfies every ValidStudy field and has mu=1/2 and HT summand variance 3/4. Choose any n>=1 and alpha in (0,1), and b=1/2 for the known-bound clause. Conditional Hoeffding for HT-muW and ordinary Hoeffding for muW-mu, followed by a union bound, give the corrected bound; bounded HT summands give the alternative. All denominators are positive almost surely.

Bounded iid summands give the two normal limits.

This verdict accepts the record's refuted decision: the theorem directly negates the canonical printed universal population-centred tail inequality. T1's valid continuous law at n=100 and alpha=10^-7 has independently verified strict noncoverage greater than alpha; the non-strict tail contains that strict event. Thus it is the printed assertion itself that is contradicted, and the docstring's 'The printed claim is false' is warranted.

W uniform, independent fair X,Y1, Y0=0, pi=m=1/2 and delta=1/4 satisfy all study hypotheses, with mu=1/2 and summand variance 3/4, so the CLT is nondegenerate. The same law permits every stored delta in (0,1/2). More generally positivity and binary outcomes bound the second moment by 1/delta, yielding a common-delta Chebyshev bound uniformly in all n>=1. The zero-outcome version also supplies the allowed zero-variance instance. Empty positivity slices at delta>=1/2 do not make the universal theorem vacuous.

Take the valid independent uniform-W/fair-X/fair-Y1 study with Y0=0, pi=m=1/2 and delta=1/4. For any n>=1 choose both fits identically zero, with any deterministic split. Every evaluated prediction is integrable, the adjusted estimator equals HT, and its expectation is mu=1/2. Lean compiled the evaluated-prediction integrability instance. The added individual integrability assumption is genuine and disclosed: cross-fold cancellation can produce an integrable final estimator even with nonintegrable individual predictions.

Use W uniform, independent fair X,Y1, Y0=0, pi=m=1/2 and delta=1/4. In part (b) use deterministic zero fits and limits g0=g1=0 with balanced half-splits; all inner errors and outer error expectations are zero and all fits are L2. This gives a misspecified, nondegenerate root-n instance. In part (d) take both deterministic fits equal to m=1/2; they are exactly L2-consistent and the Hahn variance is 1/2. The two limits in (b) are allowed to differ, as the canonical claim requires. The zero-fit L2 and mean-square predicates were also checked in Lean.

The estimator class contains the measurable identically zero sequence, as checked in Lean, and the study class contains independent uniform-W/Bernoulli-X laws. A direct argument works for every estimator: at each n>=1 put p=1/(4n), delta=p/2, W uniform, X independent Bernoulli(p), Y0=0, and compare constant Y1=0 with constant Y1=1. Both laws are valid. Their observed data agree when all treatments are zero, an event of probability (1-p)^n>=3/4. With eps=1/4 their two error probabilities sum to at least 3/4, so one is at least c=3/8. This supplies the quantifiers for arbitrarily large n. The changing positivity constant is allowed by the canonical unrestricted model; no fixed-delta construction is claimed.
